input.summary: Descriptive pilot to observe TCP flow completion time under emulated bottleneck conditions with and without 20 ms added delay. The packet contains no prior design, inputs, hashes, or resource limits, so three clarifying questions are raised and protocol is left null.
clarification_questions: What specific bottleneck parameters (bandwidth, queue size/discipline) and TCP variant should be held fixed, and what file or stream sizes define a 'flow' for this measurement?

Should the experiment use the emulated-netem-v1 runner with a specific set of pre-archived traffic traces or generate new synthetic flows, and if archived, what are the source file identities and SHA-256 hashes?
What replication count, wall-clock budget (seconds), and maximum output size (bytes) are acceptable for this pilot, and are there any exclusive hardware resources required?

proposal.problem: The packet records a claim about TCP flow completion time changing when 20 ms delay is added under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, but provides no prior design, input files, hashes, runner configuration, or resource limits.
proposal.question: Under a fixed emulated bottleneck, what TCP flow completion times are observed with 0 ms added delay versus 20 ms added delay, and how do those observed values differ across replications?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two conditions: (1) baseline — emulated bottleneck with 0 ms added one-way delay; (2) treatment — same bottleneck with 20 ms added one-way delay. All other bottleneck parameters (bandwidth, queue discipline, queue size) held constant within each replication.
proposal.related_work: The source citation is 'Synthetic networking paper claim for development evaluation' with SHA-256 aaaa…aaaa (retrieved-unreviewed); no full text or prior measurements are available for comparison.
proposal.alternatives: Observed differences in flow completion time could reflect RTT inflation, queuing interactions, TCP congestion-window dynamics, or measurement jitter; this descriptive pilot cannot distinguish among these mechanisms.
proposal.design: Paired within-replication contrast: each replication runs one baseline flow and one treatment flow under the same emulated bottleneck instance, recording flow completion time for each. Bottleneck parameters, TCP variant, and flow size remain unresolved pending owner input.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: TCP flow completion time (units: milliseconds). Secondary: per-replication difference between treatment and baseline flow completion time (milliseconds).
proposal.controls: Bottleneck bandwidth, queue discipline, queue size, TCP variant, flow size, and emulation seed are held fixed within each replication; only the added one-way delay varies between conditions.
proposal.inputs: Required inputs — emulated network topology definition, traffic flow specification (size/type), and TCP stack configuration — are not yet identified; source file identities and SHA-256 hashes are unknown and must be supplied by the owner.
proposal.limitations: No full paper text, prior measurements, input hashes, or resource limits are available. Simulation results cannot establish real-world performance or causality. Separate replications do not establish independence without a separately reviewed dependence analysis.
